title: The World's Tallest Chip Defies the Limits of Computing: Goodbye To Moore's Law?
description: Longtime Slashdot reader dbialac shares a report from EL PAIS: For decades, the progress of electronics has followed a simple rule: smaller is better. Since the 1960s, each new generation of chips has packed more transistors into less space, fulfilling the famous Moore's Law. Formulated by Intel co-founder Gordon Moore in 1965, this law predicted that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit approximately doubles each year. But this race to the minuscule is reaching its physical limits. Now, an international team of scientists is proposing a solution as obvious as it is revolutionary: if we can't keep reducing the size of chips, let's build them up.

title: Google Removed 749 Million Anna's Archive URLs From Its Search Results
description: Google has delisted over 749 million URLs from Anna's Archive, a shadow library and meta-search engine for pirated books, representing 5% of all copyright takedown requests ever filed with the company. TorrentFreak reports: Google's transparency report reveals that rightsholders asked Google to remove 784 million URLs, divided over the three main Anna's Archive domains. A small number were rejected, mainly because Google didn't index the reported links, resulting in 749 million confirmed removals. The comparison to sites such as The Pirate Bay isn't fair, as Anna's Archive has many more pages in its archive and uses multiple country-specific subdomains. This means that there's simply more content to take down.

title: Asian Stocks Pull Back Amid Tech Valuation Fears | The China Show 11/5/2025
description: “Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, David Ingles and Yvonne Man give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter.

title: APEC Leaders Walk Trump-Xi Tightrope
description: On today’s Big Take Asia podcast: On the heels of the APEC summit, how Asia’s biggest economies are navigating rising tensions between the US and China.

title: Wall Street Drops Fear of ‘Hot Commie Summer’ in Overture to Mamdani
description: New York City’s elite threw everything at Zohran Mamdani to stop him from becoming mayor: Money, insults, scare tactics, and tweets.

title: Obesity drugs may be sold at just $149 a month, get covered under Medicare under a reported White House deal in the works
description: The White House is close to announcing a deal with drugmakers Eli Lilly  and Novo Nordisk that would cut the price of obesity drugs to $149 per month in some cases and extend coverage to certain Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries, according to media reports Tuesday.

title: M&S Sees Second-Half Rebound After Cyberattack Hits Profit
description: Marks & Spencer Group Plc expects profit in the second half to rebound to at least last year’s level as the British retailer tries to move on from a costly cyberattack that disrupted sales since April.

title: Stock Pullback Has Investors Debating How Deep Selloff Will Go
description: The biggest slump in a month for US stocks is leading investors to question whether long-running concerns over lofty tech valuations, narrow market breadth and economic uncertainty will finally bring an end to the bull run that started in April.

title: China ICBC to Open Vault Boosting Hong Kong’s Gold Ambitions
description: China’s largest state-owned bank plans to open a precious metals depository at Hong Kong International Airport, offering a boost to both the lender’s trading operations and the city’s ambitions to become a global gold hub.

title: Oil Steadies as Traders Weigh US Stockpiles Against Trade Truce
description: Oil steadied as traders weighed signs of increasing US inventories against easing trade tensions between the world’s two largest economies.

title: Russia, Turkey in Talks to Keep Same Gas Volume in Renewed Deals
description: Russia and Turkey are in talks to keep up the volumes of gas supplies from Gazprom PJSC as they negotiate the renewal of two major pipeline supply deals, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: ‘It’s survival math every month’: The rent crisis that got Zohran Mamdani elected goes far beyond New York City
description: The mayor-elect built his campaign around rent affordability. But the same issue applies across the country, according to experts — and the many people struggling to pay their rent each month.

title: Upstart’s stock extends declines as the AI lender predicts slower growth
description: Upstart’s December-quarter revenue is expected to slow more than Wall Street had been modeling.

title: Stadiums, shows abroad keep Live Nation upbeat on next year after sales miss expectations
description: Live Nation Entertainment said concert demand is set to stay strong into next year, helped by shows abroad and concerts at its biggest venues. However, the Ticketmaster parent company’s third-quarter sales came up short of Wall Street’s expectations.

title: Cava trims sales outlook amid heavy competition. But it’s wary of diving into the discounting fray.
description: Mediterranean fast-casual chain Cava Group reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street’s estimates, as younger and middle-income consumers struggle with higher costs and competition remains stiff.

title: Rivian rides expiring EV credits to a revenue beat, and its stock moves higher
description: The electric-vehicle maker expects its third-quarter delivery performance to be its best of the year.
